key_insight: LLMs often fail to reliably revise clinical judgments as patient evidence changes, and prior model beliefs can unduly steer the update.
clinical_relevance: This matters because clinical AI should track evolving patient status over time, not just make a single static prediction.
method: Evaluated multiple LLMs on longitudinal ICU trajectories from electronic health records.
Tested whether predictions improved or worsened after new evidence and after prior judgments were introduced.
Used controlled prompts to isolate effects of worsening vs improving evidence and prior risk levels; also assessed an EVLU updating strategy.
evidence_signal: Across matched ICU patient trajectories, conditioning on a preceding judgment often increased rather than reduced error when estimates changed, and the pattern held on a second endpoint.
watch_item: Prompting alone did not fix the update problem, and the EVLU approach improved reliability only by reducing how often models revised their estimates.
paper_title: Large language models exhibit unreliable updating of clinical judgment as patient evidence evolves
